key_terms.meaning: An intent that names only an action (and often a data URI) and lets the system pick a matching app, so your app never touches the SMS or mail network itself.
A URI of the form smsto:+919876543210 that, sent with ACTION_SENDTO, opens the phone's SMS composer with the number already filled in.
The Android class that sends an SMS directly from your app through the phone's radio, using sendTextMessage(destination, serviceCentre, text, sentIntent, deliveryIntent).
A URI such as mailto:help@shop.in?subject=Order%20123 that pre-fills the recipient, subject and body of an e-mail in the user's mail app.
A small square image (usually 256×256 pixels) at a given zoom level and grid position that the map SDK fetches and stitches into the visible map.
A pin drawn on the map at a latitude–longitude pair, carrying an optional title, snippet and tap behaviour, used to show your own data on top of the base map.
One measured position, usually a latitude, longitude, accuracy radius in metres and a timestamp, delivered by the platform to a location callback.
A virtual circle or polygon around a real place; the app is alerted on ENTER, DWELL or EXIT when the device crosses its boundary.
The platform rule that an app can use a protected resource (SMS, contacts, camera, fine location) only after the manifest declares it and, for dangerous ones, the user grants it at runtime.
The per-app isolation in which each app runs as its own user ID with its own private data directory, so one app cannot read another's files.
A hardware-backed system service that stores private keys and secrets so they can be used for signing or encryption without the key value ever leaving protected storage.
The client accepts only a specific server certificate or public key instead of any certificate a trusted authority signs, which blocks man-in-the-middle attacks using a rogue but valid certificate.
Stored data — files, databases, cached tokens on the device or on a server — protected by encryption, Keystore-held keys and app-private storage.
Data moving over the network, protected by TLS with a valid certificate and, ideally, certificate pinning.
The rule that an app requests only the permissions and scopes it actually uses, for the shortest time, so an exploited app damages less.
A server- or admin-triggered command that erases corporate data, or the whole device, after loss, theft or an employee leaving.
The build variant signed with your release key, with debug logging off and code shrunk, that you may distribute; a debug APK must never be published.
A .jks file holding the private key that identifies the app to the store and to the device; losing it blocks all future updates under the same package name.
Buying and selling goods and services through a mobile device, including in-app purchases, mobile web stores and mobile wallets.
The service between merchant and bank that encrypts and routes the payment request, performs authentication and returns an authorisation result to the app.

takeaways: An app should hand an SMS or e-mail to the phone's own app with an implicit intent unless the business case truly needs silent, server-side sending.
A map screen is just a view that draws server-supplied tiles plus your markers, and every marker is a latitude–longitude pair you already hold.
Location data is a trade-off between accuracy and battery, so pick a provider and an update interval that match the job.
Geofencing moves the work from your app to the platform: you register a fence and wait for ENTER, DWELL or EXIT callbacks.
Mobile security has layers — device, network, app — and every layer needs its own control: permission system, TLS with pinning, app sandbox and Keystore.
Least privilege is the cheapest security control: every permission you do not request is a permission that cannot be abused.
Publishing is a fixed sequence: version, shrink, sign with the release keystore, align, test the release build, then upload or distribute.
In m-commerce the app is only one link in a chain of customer, merchant, gateway and bank, and the gateway fee decides net revenue.
bank_note: Long answers here usually ask you to wire up the SMS and e-mail intents, explain how maps and location updates are built, list publishing steps in order, and then compare m-commerce payment models while naming the security control used at each layer.

bank.q: Explain the two ways an Android app can send an SMS: through the phone's messaging app with an intent, and directly with SmsManager. Give the call or intent for each and state when each is the right choice.
outline: ACTION_SENDTO with a smsto: URI opens the SMS composer; the user presses send
smsto: URI format and how the body is pre-filled (smsto:number with sms_body extra)
SmsManager.sendTextMessage(destination, serviceCentre, text, sentIntent, deliveryIntent) sends silently
SEND_SMS is a dangerous permission granted at runtime
Intent route needs no SMS permission; direct route needs it and costs money per message
Use the intent route for user-composed messages; use SmsManager only for app-generated alerts with clear consent

bank.q: Describe how a map is drawn inside an app screen. Cover map tiles, zoom levels, the camera position, and how your own data appears on top.
outline: Map SDK authenticates with an API key and fetches tiles from the map provider
A tile is a 256×256 image identified by zoom level z and tile coordinates x, y
The view stitches tiles, then draws overlays such as markers and shapes
Camera position is latitude, longitude and zoom; moving the camera triggers new tile fetches
A marker is created from a LatLng plus title and snippet and added to the map object
Data flow: your database or API gives coordinates, the SDK does all rendering

bank.q: Explain how an app gets and monitors location data. Compare GPS, network and fused providers on accuracy, indoor behaviour and battery use.
outline: Location is latitude, longitude, accuracy in metres, altitude and time
GPS provider: metre-level outdoors, slow first fix, high battery drain, poor indoors
Network provider: cell and Wi-Fi based, fast, coarse, works indoors
Fused provider merges sensors and is preferred on modern Android
Permission levels: coarse vs fine location; runtime request
Monitoring: requestLocationUpdates with interval and minimum distance, or a single getCurrentLocation
Always stop updates in onPause/onStop to save battery

bank.q: List the layers of mobile security (device, network, app layer, app sandbox) and give one concrete control used at each layer.
outline: Device layer: screen lock, full-disk encryption, remote wipe, OS updates
Network layer: TLS for data in transit, certificate pinning, avoiding open Wi-Fi for payments
App layer: permission system and runtime permission checks, input validation, no secrets in code
App sandbox: per-app user ID and private data directory, signature-based sharing
Data at rest protection with Keystore-held keys
Least privilege as the thread running through every layer

bank.q: A shop-finder app must let a user send a chosen shop's address to a friend by SMS and show the shop on a map. Describe the screen flow, the intents and map calls you would use, and the permissions needed.
outline: Tap on marker opens an info window with a Share action
Share builds a message string with shop name and address or a maps link
ACTION_SENDTO with smsto: URI and sms_body extra launches the messaging app, so no SEND_SMS permission
Fallback: ACTION_SEND with type text/plain to let the user pick SMS, e-mail or chat
Map: create MapView/SupportMapFragment, obtain the map object, move camera to the shop LatLng, add Marker
Load shop list from API, build LatLng per shop, clear old markers on refresh
Permissions: INTERNET, location only if you centre on the user

bank.q: Describe, step by step, how you prepare an Android app for publishing and deploy the APK. Include versioning, shrinking, signing and testing.
outline: Set applicationId and remove debug flags and test servers
Set versionCode (integer, must increase every release) and versionName (user-visible string)
Enable minifyEnabled and shrinkResources with R8/ProGuard rules
Create a signing keystore, keep it and its passwords safe and out of version control
Configure the release signingConfig and build the release variant
Run zipalign so resources are aligned for lower memory use
Verify the signature with apksigner
Test the signed release build on a real device, including upgrade from the previous version
Deploy via Play Console upload (AAB or APK) or direct APK install with unknown sources allowed

bank.q: A shopping app accepts card and UPI payments. Trace a payment from the tap on Pay to the confirmation screen, naming each party, and show how gateway fees affect net revenue on a ₹1,000 order.
outline: Customer, merchant app, payment gateway, acquiring bank, card network or UPI switch, issuing bank
App sends an encrypted payment token, never the raw card number, so the app stays out of PCI scope
Gateway performs 3-D Secure or UPI PIN authentication and returns success or failure
Response handling: verify signature or server callback, never trust the app-side result alone
Fees: say 2% gateway charge and 18% GST on the fee
On ₹1,000: fee ₹20, GST ₹3.60, net ₹976.40 before other costs
Refunds and failed-payment reversals also carry cost, so net revenue is lower

bank.q: You must add live location tracking to a delivery app. Show how to use the permission system and location APIs with least privilege and acceptable battery use.
outline: Ask for fine location only when the user starts tracking; explain why before the dialog
Handle denial and 'don't ask again' with a fallback such as manual address entry
Foreground service with a visible notification for tracking while the app is backgrounded
LocationRequest with a chosen interval and smallest displacement; raise the interval when the vehicle is not moving
Remove updates when tracking stops; release the service
Send fixes to the server over TLS, do not log coordinates
Do not collect background location for a feature that only needs a one-time fix

bank.q: Explain how you would protect a login token and a payment response in a mobile app, using the Android Keystore, data-at-rest encryption and certificate pinning. Show the flow in order.
outline: Generate or import an AES key in the Android Keystore; the key material never leaves it
Encrypt the token with that key and store only the ciphertext and IV in app-private storage
Use EncryptedSharedPreferences or equivalent for small secrets
Data in transit: HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher, then pin the server public key or certificate
Pin via network security config or a custom TrustManager; include a backup pin for rotation
Reject connections on pin mismatch and fail closed
Never hard-code API secrets in the APK; they can be extracted

bank.q: Analyse the security risks in a mobile wallet app and map each risk to the OWASP Mobile Top 10 category and a control.
outline: Improper credential usage: hard-coded keys in the APK; move secrets to the server or Keystore
Insecure data storage: plain token in external storage; encrypt at rest, keep app-private
Insecure communication: HTTP endpoints; enforce TLS and pinning
Insufficient cryptography: ECB mode or fixed IV; use AES-GCM with random IV
Insecure authentication: no session timeout or no device binding; add biometric or PIN re-auth
Code tampering and reverse engineering: R8 obfuscation, integrity checks, Play Integrity API
Extraneous functionality: leftover debug endpoints and logs must be removed

bank.q: Your app must deliver a one-time password. Evaluate four options — SMS intent, own SMS gateway, e-mail intent, push notification — on reliability, cost, security and user friction, and recommend one.
outline: SMS intent: free, user-visible, but user may not send it and it is unreliable for OTP delivery
Own SMS gateway: costs per message in rupees, needs a server and DLT registration in India, high reach
E-mail intent: no cost, but slow delivery and users may not check mail in time
Push notification: free and fast but needs network, app installed and notification permission
Security: OTP must have short validity, be bound to one session and never be logged
Recommendation: server-side SMS gateway or its verified API for OTP, push for non-critical alerts, and never rely on the user tapping send

bank.q: A retail chain wants an app that sends discount offers when a customer enters a mall. Evaluate the location design and the privacy trade-offs, and state the checks you would build in.
outline: Geofence per mall registered with the platform; ENTER triggers the offer
Dwell and EXIT used to avoid repeat spam
Trade-off: background location and constant scanning cost battery; use a coarse radius and few fences
Privacy: collect only the fence ID, not a continuous track; ask consent in plain language
Permission system: background location is a separate, stricter grant; provide an opt-out
Store data for a short retention period and avoid linking to identity where possible
Legal compliance and clear notice; the business benefit must justify each data point

bank.q: Compare a debug build and a release build of the same app, and analyse what goes wrong if a release is signed with a leaked or lost keystore.
outline: Debug: debuggable flag set, debug key, no shrinking, logs on, larger APK
Release: signed with your key, R8 shrinking and obfuscation, logs stripped, smaller and faster
Lost keystore: cannot publish updates under the same applicationId; only a new package name and loss of install base
Leaked keystore with password: attackers can ship a malicious update that the device accepts as genuine
Mitigation: store the keystore offline or in a managed vault, use Play App Signing so the upload key can be reset
Rotate keys if compromise is suspected and keep a strong password

glossary.def: Intent action that means 'send a message to this URI', used with smsto:, mailto: or tel: URIs and handled by another app.
Intent action that shares content of a given MIME type, letting the user pick any app that can accept it.
The intent extra key that carries the pre-filled text of an SMS when the SMS composer is opened.
Android class that sends and divides long SMS messages directly over the phone radio, requiring the SEND_SMS permission.
A location API that merges GPS, Wi-Fi and sensor signals to give better accuracy at lower battery cost than any single provider.
A source of position fixes such as GPS, network or passive, each with its own accuracy, speed and power profile.
A permission the app must request from the user while running, because it protects a dangerous resource such as location or SMS.
A permission class in Android that gives access to private user data or device control and therefore needs explicit user consent.
The AndroidManifest.xml file that declares the app's package, components, permissions and hardware features.
The latitude, longitude, zoom and tilt that define what a map view is currently showing.
The map provider's service that returns map tile images for a zoom level and tile coordinate.
OWASP's ranked list of the most common mobile app security risks, used as a checklist during design and testing.
Data stored on the device or server, protected by encryption and access control.
Data travelling across a network, protected by TLS and optionally certificate pinning.
Giving an app or a user the smallest set of rights needed for the current task, and no more.
The isolation boundary where each app gets its own Linux user ID and private storage, limiting damage if it is compromised.
A system service that holds cryptographic keys in protected storage and performs operations without exposing key material.
Restricting which server certificate or public key the client will trust, defeating man-in-the-middle attacks with forged certificates.
A command from a management server that erases device or work-profile data after loss, theft or employee exit.
Tools that shrink, optimise and obfuscate class names in a release build, reducing APK size and raising the effort to reverse engineer.
An integer in the manifest that must increase with every store release; the platform uses it to decide which build is newer.
The user-visible version string such as 2.4.1 shown in the store listing and the app's About screen.
The unique package name that identifies the app on a device and in a store, and the identity that signing protects.
A build step that aligns uncompressed resources on 4-byte boundaries so Android can memory-map them efficiently.
The percentage fee a merchant pays on each card or wallet transaction, covering gateway, network and bank charges.
India's Unified Payments Interface, which lets a mobile app send a payment request to a bank account through a virtual payment address.
